edges.effect_quant: Systematic reviews drawing on randomized studies suggest a small average effect that is directionally consistent but not dramatic.
edges.mechanism: This factor changes substrate delivery, microbial competition, short-chain fatty-acid production, or early-life colonization patterns in the gut. Those changes are most directly linked to Irritable bowel syndrome when the endpoint is microbial composition, barrier function, or a gut-mediated immune phenotype.
edges.summary: The strongest gut-related effects usually appear in intermediate outcomes such as fermentation products, stool features, or symptom scores rather than sweeping microbiome reset claims. Systematic reviews drawing on randomized studies link psyllium to lower risk of irritable bowel syndrome in adults with IBS. The average effect is usually small rather than dramatic, so this edge is better read as a risk modifier than a stand-alone cause or cure.
edges.caveats: Dose, timing, and baseline risk still matter. Observational edges may partly reflect broader lifestyle patterning, while small trials can overstate benefit if follow-up is short.
